handbook.title: The IoT Engineering Handbook
handbook.subtitle: Engineering connected devices, physical effects and trustworthy evidence
handbook.description: Learn IoT engineering through connected-system models, physical observation, fault diagnosis and a Go/TinyGo lab with explicit evidence limits.
handbook.intro: A handbook for engineers connecting software to the physical world. Start with what a connected system can know, then follow commands, observations and faults across the boundary. Chapter 1 is available as a draft; its physical lab and independent review are pending.

chapters.title: What Is an IoT System, Really?
chapters.subtitle: Belief, command, effect and observation
chapters.description: Trace an IoT system from software belief to physical evidence, diagnose a real fan wiring fault, and explore a Go/TinyGo LED lab.
chapters.outcome: you can distinguish a software acknowledgement from evidence of a physical effect.
chapters.prerequisiteText: Comfort with Go code. No electronics experience required.
